gaps.sentence: The recipe ___ (pass down) from generation to generation.
gaps.hint: continuing relevance from past to now
gaps.explanation: Present perfect passive: has been + passed down; the process links past and present.

gaps.sentence: Several issues remain ___ (resolve) before the launch.
gaps.explanation: 'Remain' + passive infinitive (to be resolved) expresses unfinished business.

gaps.sentence: The original manuscript ___ (lose) for over a century.
gaps.hint: state resulting from a past passive action
gaps.explanation: Past simple passive: was + lost. The person who lost it is unknown or unimportant.

gaps.sentence: The divers ___ (know) to have been working without insurance.
gaps.explanation: are known to have been working: the knowing is present, the working was ongoing before.

gaps.sentence: By this time tomorrow, the results ___ to every candidate.
gaps.explanation: 'By this time tomorrow' requires future perfect passive: will have been + emailed.

gaps.sentence: The new stadium ___ by the end of the decade.
gaps.explanation: 'By the end of the decade' needs future perfect passive: will have been + completed. The stadium is completed by somebody.

gaps.sentence: Hamlet ___ (perform) almost continuously since it was written.
gaps.explanation: 'Since + past clause' requires present perfect passive: has been + performed.

gaps.sentence: The ancient scrolls are far too brittle ___ .
gaps.explanation: The scrolls receive the action: passive infinitive to be + unrolled.
